subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equation to the pair of transverse common tangents to the circles x² + y² − 4x − 10y + 28 = 0 and x² + y² + 4x − 6y + 4 = 0.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, SENIOR INTER MATHS-2B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.21 — LAQ chapter 1 Circle, answer 7. Printed appearance tags: AP 19 and TS 17,19. The mark split is OURS, not the book’s: this answer sits on a two-column page with no printed margin tags. It is patterned on the nearest printed split of the same shape in this chapter — book p.16, answer 3, which prints 1 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 1 for the same two-equations-then-centre-then-circle shape, and book p.17, answer 4, which prints 1 + 1 + 1 + 4. Star rank: the book gives the CIRCLE LAQ chapter ★★★ in its LAQ chapter table (book p.13), in the chapter header (book p.14) and in the LAQ hit list header (book p.7), so every Circle LAQ entry takes stars 3. An LAQ on this paper is 7 marks, never 8 — the 2026-27 move to 8-mark long answers is first year only. Every number was re-derived and the book is correct: I = (1, 9/2), S₁ = −x − y/2 + 7/2, S₁₁ = 1/4, and the pair is 3x² + 4xy − 24x − 4y + 21 = 0 with no y² term, which is correct here and not an omission. insider_note: The final pair has no y² term at all, which looks like a mistake but is not — one of the two tangents is vertical in effect, and a student who "corrects" it by inserting a y² term loses the answer.

steps.label: Centres and radii
steps.margin_note: One mark. Both radii are whole numbers here, so the ratio 1 : 3 is exact.
steps.memory_tip: Read g, f, c off each equation; the radius is √(g² + f² − c) every time.
steps.why: Transverse common tangents cross between the circles, so the circles must lie apart. The centres and radii are what the crossing point is built from.
common_mistakes: Reading g = −4 instead of g = −2 for the first circle.
Getting r₁ = √57 by adding 28 instead of subtracting it.

steps.label: Internal centre of similitude
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Transverse tangents use INTERNAL division — the crossing point sits between the two centres.
steps.memory_tip: Transverse tangents cross between the circles, so their meeting point divides C₁C₂ internally.
lines: The internal centre of similitude I divides
steps.why: Both transverse tangents pass through one point between the circles, and that point divides the line of centres internally in the ratio of the radii. Every later step is measured from it.
common_mistakes: Using external division, which gives the direct tangents.

steps.label: Pair of tangents from I
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Either circle may be used for S; the first one is chosen because its radius is 1.
steps.memory_tip: The pair of tangents from a point to a circle is S₁² = S₁₁ · S. Compute S₁ and S₁₁ separately, then combine.
lines: The pair of tangents from I(x₁, y₁) to
steps.why: S₁ is the general form with one point replaced by I, and S₁₁ is S₁ with both points equal to I. Because I lies outside the circle, S₁₁ is positive and the pair is a genuine pair of lines.
common_mistakes: Writing S₁ with g and f not halved, giving −4(x + 1) instead of −2(x + 1).
Getting S₁₁ = 0 by an arithmetic slip, which would say I is on the circle.

steps.label: Simplify to the pair equation
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. Clear the halves first by writing S₁ over 2, then square.
steps.memory_tip: Write −x − y/2 + 7/2 as (−2x − y + 7)/2 so the square is a clean quarter.
steps.why: The quarter on each side cancels. The y² terms are equal on both sides and cancel as well, so the final pair has no y² term — that is correct, not an omission, and it says one of the two tangents is parallel to the y-axis in the pair’s coordinate reading.
common_mistakes: Expanding (2x + y − 7)² without the cross terms 4xy, −28x and −14y.
Inserting a y² term into the final answer because a pair "should" have one.

steps.label: The picture
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own; the question does not ask for a diagram. Draw it in rough to confirm the division is internal.
steps.memory_tip: Transverse tangents cross between the circles. Direct tangents do not.

elements.text: transverse common tangents cross at I

steps.why: The two transverse tangents put the circles on opposite sides of each line, so they must cross between the circles, at I. Seeing that is what fixes the division as internal rather than external.
common_mistakes: Drawing the tangents meeting outside both circles, which is the direct case.
Drawing circles that overlap, in which case no transverse tangent exists.
